One of the common issues I've been seeing with these newer machines are the difficulties that come with installing a clean OS. Some of the BIOs that I've worked (Lenovo, HP, ASUS) that come pre-installed with Windows 8 sometimes lock the ability to do a clean install. Usually the first thing I do is replace 8 with 7.

Are there any machines that are less strict on their BIOs booting different operating systems? I've been looking for a new laptop/netbook that I could do a dual install of 7 and Arch Linux without having to worry about the BIOs locking up that feature.
Have you noticed newer laptops having BIOs issues that make it difficult to perform a clean OS install?

You need media to do a clean install. Some manufacturers will include a recovery partition (Lenovo), or allow you to create recovery discs (Dell). Although these recovery partitions and media creation utilities will not give you a "clean install". They will still load the bloat-ware that comes with the manufacturer's pre-loaded OS.

The BIOS (Basic input/output system) doesn't restrict anything beyond booting to specific types of media. In some cases, disabling UEFI can help if you're having difficulties booting an OS install from a USB drive.

If you want to install a dinosaur like Windows 7 on to your computer, you will need the installation discs. Or, burn your installation media to an ISO which you can then create a bootable flash drive with in order to continue.

You could also just load a side-by-side OS and choose Windows 7 from pre-os as a menu option as opposed to Windows 8. This way, you still have the older operating system for your outdated, perhaps proprietary, software, as well as the option to boot to the more robust, feature-rich Windows 8.

tl;dr: You need installation media.

I hope this helps!!

edit: clarification on manufacturer media. added tl;dr
Are you having UEFI issues? Stand alone BIOS is going the way of the floppy drive.

You're talking about Secure Boot. It's new with Windows 8, and does, in fact, involve the BIOS. I recently fixed an HP laptop for a friend. The HDD had failed, so I bought a new SSD to replace it. After I installed Windows 8 (the same as the original OS, before the drive broke), however, I couldn't boot until I disabled Secure Boot. So it's definitely not a recovery partition—those are stored on the drive, of course, not in BIOS. As long as your BIOS allows you to disable it, you shouldn't need to worry. It's kind of a pain, though.
